body: I wanted to post a negative review only to warn people of something that happened to me with these gummies as I combined them with another magnesium supplement. I suffer from hot flashes in menopause and was told to try Magnesium L-Threonate. So I studied up on my Magnesium knowledge and mixed it with Magnesium Glycinate thinking both would help relieve my hot flashes and help me relax. Well, in theory I thought it would work. I was in a hurry to get to work one morning and took two of the L-Threonate and one of the Glycinate on an empty stomach and drove to work. About 30 minutes later, I was dizzy, disoriented, my vision was fluttering (that's how it felt) and I felt like my blood sugar was low. My face was hot and I felt like I might be having a stroke. I'm 54 and in good health, so I didn't know what to do. I quickly purchase an orange juice, drank half a glass and sat down. It took a good 10 minutes for the dizziness and vision to return to normal. I am not a health professional but I want to warn people about too much Magnesium. If you have a balanced diet and get natural magnesium through your foods, be careful of dosages for these supplements. They are not candy although they taste great. So don't give them to your kids unless they need it and don't take them on an empty stomach. I have a lower blood pressure already and they really dropped my blood sugar. Do your homework and they didn't help my hot flashes. I know everyone is different but I thought I'd leave this warning. I read some of the 1 star reviews for this product and they do work! Especially in high doses! Do research, you can overdose on Magnesium!

body: These are Magnesium Glycinate gummies. Magnesium glycinate is an excellent form of magnesium to use as a supplement as it is very well absorbed in contrast to many of the traditional Mg supplements such as Mg Oxide or even Mg citrate. The label states that (two gummies) provides 600 mg of Mg glycinate. While the may be accurate, it seems a tiny bit deceptive to me, as Mg glycinate is only 14.1% elemental magnesium. Each gummy contains about 42 mg of elemental magnesium, one tenth of the RDA for for Magnesium for a man. Two gummies should provide 84 mg of magnesium. This may be sufficient a dose to boost magnesium some, but falls short of common therapeutic recommendations for sleep, relaxation, etc. The quality control of the gummies is marginal. The orange ones are soft and like a gummy candy but the yellow and red ones are crystallized and a bit hard on the outside. They are unpleasantly sweet - something I rarely say. They are sweetened with sugar and maltitol. They are listed as containing "color added" but it does not specify if it is natural color. The gummies are made with pectin so I assume they are vegan. The manufacture date (11/03/2025 seven months in the future - indicates they are using MDY dating system which is used in Europe and Latin America, and thus, they are not made in the U.S. (and probably not in China).

body: I'm really cautious regarding supplements I ingest, and I try to order brands that are clear and open about their products. There are so many xyz alphabet soup companies bringing new products with unknown sourcing to the market today, and consumers must do their due diligence. Thus, I ordered the Inner Brightness Magnesium Glycinate gummies because they are advertised as Made in USA in the seller's Amazon photos. Well, the bottle I received has no such markings, anywhere. The label does indicate the Inner Brightness brand is distributed by Soartech LLC. in Washington state. So I went to the seller's/distributor's website as listed on the label. In the About Us section is a photo of the US manufacturing facility, Reaps Pharma, Inc, that is said to manufacture the vitamins for Soartech LLC. When I do an internet search for Reaps Pharma, Inc. in California, however, I'm brought to a website that is lacking in information - when I try to read about the services or products they provide, such as Our Core Services, I can't click any further, none of the links expands to give me information, such as Certificates of Analysis, Lab Certifications, etc. The internet research shows a lot of links in Chinese script, so I'm not exactly sure of the sourcing of this product. Further, there is more than one place on the seller's Amazon ad - and the front and back of the product label - that says 600 mg of Magnesium Glycinate per serving. Doing the math, however, the back label shows that a serving of 2 gummies = 100 mg of Magnesium. I am questioning how there can be 600 mg of Magnesium Glycinate squeezed out of 100 mg of Magnesium. The math does not add up. Based on the misleading information in the seller's Amazon photos and description, and the lack of clarity about if this product is truly made in the USA, I would not order it again.

body: Please read this before buying if you need a true, therapeutic dose of magnesium. The label on this product is a direct violation of FDA supplement regulations and presents a physical impossibility.The front of the bottle and the Supplement Facts grid claim you are getting "400 mg of Magnesium (as magnesium glycinate)" in a single gummy serving. Pure magnesium glycinate is a very bulky molecule that is only about 14% elemental magnesium by weight. To actually get a genuine 400 mg of elemental magnesium, a manufacturer would have to pack roughly 2,857 mg (nearly 3 grams) of raw powder into the recipe. A standard gummy candy only weighs about 2 to 3 grams in total. If this label were accurate, the gummy would be a hard, dry block of solid white chalk with absolutely zero physical room left for gelatin, water, sweeteners, or raspberry flavoring.What this company is actually doing is writing the weight of their total compound powder blend on the "Magnesium" line. Industry watchdogs (like NOW Foods) have repeatedly busted unverified online brands for this exact deceptive practice. In reality, a single Pura Wex gummy only gives you about 56 mg of actual, elemental magnesium.To get the 400 mg dose advertised on the bottle, you would have to eat 7 gummies a day. Doing that would overload your system with sugars and gelling binders, causing severe stomach cramps, nausea, and diarrhea. If you are taking this to correct a deficiency or to balance a specific medication/peptide protocol, you are going to be severely under-dosed. Avoid this brand and buy solid, third-party tested capsules or tablets from a reputable manufacturer instead.
